answer: Weight each agent vote by coins locked for the entire dispute, with no per-account bonus and no reuse of locked coins across concurrent disputes. Agents judging whether a traded plume came from a falcon or was dyed with saffron must lock funds before voting. A ledger snapshot assigns one vote per locked coin: splitting 100 coins among ten identities still yields only 100 votes. Each extra vote needs another locked coin. This blocks alias-based amplification, not domination by wealthy voters.
